El el mensaje sostiene que "con respecto al trámite de renovación de la Visa Americana, son cosas que ya nos han sucedido en el pasado".

Trascendió que la visa de turista se le vence en estos primeros meses del año, por lo que Char inició los trámites y fue cuando recibió la negativa.

Cabe recordar que al padre del exalcalde de Barranquilla, el empresario Fuad Char Abdala también le fue negada la entrada a los Estados Unidos en 1994, cuando era Senador de la República.

En aquella ocasión Fuad Char necesitaba viajar para visitar a su su esposa Adela Chaljub, quien recibía atención médica por una grave enfermedad.

#GivingTuesday
As we continue to grow and thrive as a community, it is important that we all do our part to support our church financially. One of the most important ways that we can do this is by committing to regular tithing and gift offering.

Tithing is the act of giving a tenth of our income to the church. It is a biblical principle that has been practiced for centuries, and it is a powerful way for us to support the work of the church and further the kingdom of God.

We understand that sometimes tithing can be a difficult commitment to make, especially in today's uncertain economic climate. However, we believe that it is a small sacrifice that can have a big impact on the future of our church. By tithing and  donating, we are investing in the future of our church and the kingdom of God.

If you have any questions or concerns about tithing, please don't hesitate to reach out to one of our church leaders or pastor. We are here to support and encourage you in your giving.

Vigil Mass for Life – Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception –

Did you ever wonder why the Sisters of Life sit in ‘invented pews’ in front of the front pews of the Vigil Mass for Life?

I don’t.

I’ve seen them kneel in prayer on the filthy streets of the South Bronx

Brooklyn…

Manhattan…

Ridiculed, insulted…

Never backing down.

They ARE the front line defending the lives of the most vulnerable.

Supporting, embracing, and empowering women carrying those precious lives within them

Standing armed with love and compassion.

With strength and courage.

With Faith.

So if there was a place of honor for them, it might be in those ‘invented pews’

But not because it’s prestigious

But because it’s closer to Christ, to Whom they are espoused

To Whom they serve

Not that you were asking, but that’s my answer

The special day at school made Riley feel happy, special and loved. There are too many sad and bad days during a pediatric cancer journey. Riley loves school, and loves learning new things. Riley is going to be upset about missing school when she has surgery.
Please keep Riley Faith and her family in your prayers!

Casual food content. Can you shoot it? Do you find it challenging? 

I was asked to shoot some ‘casual’ food content for one of my clients, the idea was to depict a relaxed home atmosphere, eating while sitting on the couch or floor. Not the usual staged studio content ;)

It’s definitely good to have such shots in your portfolio,it shows your potential clients that you can accommodate such requests.

What can be challenging with such shoots:

-dependance on and availability of the model. That can be replaced by photographing yourself in the frame with your camera connected via WIFI to your phone which allows you to see the whole scene and apply the right focus.

-the right light! When photographing yourself while sitting on the floor can be tricky if you don’t have the availability of a big enough light source, e.g floor to ceiling window that will ensure the right amount of light coming into your scene. Never Late

Read : John 11:17–27

Your brother will rise again. John 11:23

As a visitor to a small West African town, my American pastor made sure to arrive on time for a 10 a.m. Sunday service. Inside the humble sanctuary, however, he found the room empty. So he waited. One hour. Two hours. Finally, about 12:30 p.m., when the local pastor arrived after his long walk there—followed by some choir members and a gathering of friendly town people—the service began “in the fullness of time,” as my pastor later said. “The Spirit welcomed us, and God wasn’t late.” My pastor understood the culture was different here for its own good reasons.

Time seems relative, but God’s perfect, on-time nature is affirmed throughout the Scriptures. Thus, after Lazarus got sick and died, Jesus arrived four days later, with Lazarus’ sisters asking why. “Lord,” Martha said to Jesus, “if you had been here, my brother would not have died” (John 11:21). We are all different and we want/need different things. Especially during the holidays, there is a lot of social pressure to do what is traditional or "expected." But it does not work for everyone.
.
Please take a moment to consider your neurodivergent loved ones, children and adults. There are things you can do to make sure that they enjoy the holidays.
.
- ask them about their preferences, wants, and needs
- listen with an open mind
- ask what they need to be comfortable
- ask how you can support them
- talk about different aspects of the holiday: food, gifts, sensory environment, size of parties, location of celebration, etc. It is important to think through details
- don't take their preferences personally. It might be hard to hear that your loved one needs more alone time or does not want to go to big gatherings with you. Please keep in mind that this is not because they do not like you. It is because they trust to tell you what they truly need
.
Have a wonderful holiday season!
.

Jesus is the best gift! 

I love this statement from the Christmas Gift freebie printablefrom Faith Heirlooms. It really touches my heart and releases me from the heavy weight of commercialism promoted and required by modern culture.  This season is about HIM. 

Two tips from this page:
1. Use the printable as a teaching guide.  I wanted the name of Jesus larger, so I used the word on the printable as a guide using a gold pen and then trace the other words. 
2. Alter the doll to fit your page.  Since I took up so much space with my words, I had less space for the girl. First I (temporarily) cut off her legs and affixed them to the page.  Then I trimmed her hair slightly and shortened her dress.  Ta-da!

This is a post I do every year around holiday time. I have expanded it this year to offer more information and detail. 
.
Our autistic loved ones process information differently. When we give gifts, it is important that we keep that in mind and give in ways that are comfortable and will result in a good experience. This means that we need to adjust what we give, how we give, and what reaction we expect. 
.
Please keep in mind that each autistic person is different. No advice will apply to everyone. 
.
What is important is that we accept and respect the differences. There is no wrong way to enjoy the holidays. 
.
I wish each one of you and your loved ones a joyful, enjoyable, and safe holiday season! 
.
Please comment: do you have strategies or insights to add about giving gifts?
.
Warmly, Yulika aka The Expert Ally
.
And special thanks to you if you also decide to buy gifts for Ukrainian autistic children (see the last slide). 
.

?Shake a tail Feather! 
On a bit of a ‘super tiny things’ run at the moment so here’s another to chuck in. This little fluff ball even out tinied the peacock spiders - I want to say it was a millimetre, but let’s just say it’s 2 to be sure. On a leaf this lil fella just looked like a piece of lint or hoodie fluff, I wouldn’t have even known it was living if it hadn’t of been moving. 

Like a lot of things this small, it’s took firing off a couple shots, checking the camera preview and zooming in to realise how crazy cool it was. The ass-end of this hopper has this mad kind of candy floss thing going on. Hard to know what it’s purpose is really, but I was determined to try and get a good enough stack to highlight all the little ‘spines’. Glad that one of my 2 or 3 attempts came out pretty well before it lived up to its names sake and hopped well outta sight.

Allah calls Himself Al-Fattaah— The Opener, The Revealer— on one occasion in the Quran. He is the One who opens all doors of blessing for His slaves. Al-Fattaah judges what shall be opened from opening hearts, clarifying visions and opening doors to sustenance to conquering cities and revealing knowledge!
.
The Judge of All That is Opened, The Granter of Success
.
Fattaah comes from the root faa-taa-haa, which points to four main meanings. The first main meaning is to open, unlock, or reveal and make clear. The second main meaning is to make victorious, and the third is to judge or decide. The fourth main meaning is to permit or grant.
.
This root appears 38 times in the Quran in eight derived forms. Examples of these forms are fatahnaa (“We opened”), al-fathu (“the victory”), and mafaatihu (“[are the] keys”).
.
